policies.acceptance: Session-481 accepted the design at Step 3 (comm-008805) and the six plan files at Step 5 (comm-008807, reviewDecision accept, needs_revision=false). The design edits, the plans and this manifest are committed together in the plan checkpoint commit before fanout.
policies.evidencePolicy: A behavioral record is a test-runner command (bun test ... or vitest run ...) with exit code 0 and a test count greater than 0. cd web && bun test src and cd web && bunx vitest run are recorded separately. mise run web:check is never the recorded test command, though it may be run as an extra record. Tee every command into the plan's evidence directory and record the complete log path and the final exit status. An incomplete log is not a pass.
policies.evidenceLayout: Evidence lives under tmp/tauri-client-connection/<P#> (P1..P5), gitignored through tmp/. P5 writes command logs under tmp/tauri-client-connection/P5/logs/ and its summary in tmp/tauri-client-connection/P5/evidence.md. Each plan keeps its own intent.md, hashes.txt and progress.md, and never writes another plan's evidence directory.
policies.editProtocol: Follow the index 'Edit protocol': write an immutable intent.md before the first edit, record pre/post shasum -a 256 per edit in hashes.txt, re-read and re-apply only your own intent on drift, and edit only your own writePaths. A peer plan's compile or lint failure is not a blocker; record it for serial reconciliation (P5). No git write operations, no branches or worktrees, and no edits to .riela/ or node_modules/ beyond the declared vitest cache artifact root.
policies.artifactPolicy: Artifact roots are copied unchanged from the accepted plans: P3 declares web/node_modules/.vite; P5 declares tmp/tauri-client-connection/P5/logs, web/src-tauri/target, web/src-tauri/local-service, web/src-tauri/gen/schemas, web/dist, .build and web/node_modules/.vite. All are gitignored. P1, P2 and P4 declare none.
policies.protectedPaths: No plan edits Sources/, Package.swift, Package.resolved, web/src-tauri/src/, web/src-tauri/capabilities/, web/src-tauri/tauri*.conf.json, scripts/, mise.toml, any CSS file, schema/note-store.sqlite.sql, Sources/AppCore/NoteStoreSchemaDDL.generated.swift, .riela/, or any impl-plans/active/*-dispatch.json. P4 may edit only the dangling word in design-docs/specs/tauri-client-apps.md.
policies.storePolicy: Never read, open or launch against the real macOS app store (Application Support/com.tacogips.kaiba/local under the user's home) or the default kaiba store. Do not launch Kaiba.app, its binaries, or kaiba serve with default paths.
policies.releasePolicy: No signing, notarization, release publishing, tag, cask, tap or git push. The deliverable is an unsigned local Kaiba.app build output.

reviewContext.issueReference: workflowInput issue (no GitHub URL/number): 'Tauri client app with configurable connection target' (user request 2026-10-25); targetFeatureArea=tauri-client-connection; design accepted at Step 3 (comm-008805); plans accepted at Step 5 (comm-008807)
reviewContext.userProblem: The user wants the macOS Kaiba Tauri client built from current main, and wants its connection target (Local bundled server or a remote URL) easy to configure, testable before switching, remembered across recent servers, and reachable even when the current server is unreachable, erroring or requires sign-in.
requiredOutcomes: P1: serverEndpoint.ts gains readRecentServerEndpoints, recordRecentServerEndpoint (bound 5, normalized origins, defensive read, never touches credential keys), isUnencryptedRemoteEndpoint and activeConnectionLabel, with bun tests.

P2: new serverProbe.ts with testServerConnection (GET /healthz then POST /graphql, 5 s abort, no Authorization header, assertServerOrigin on both targets, savedCredential as presence check only) and describeServerProbe with pinned sentences, with bun tests.

P3: ServerConnectionSettings shows the active connection line, a Test connection button, a Recent servers picker and a plain-http warning; a successful Remote save records the recent entry; ConnectionReachability.integration.tsx proves the form is reachable from network-error and 401 states.
P4: README 'macOS and iPhone clients' describes the new controls; the dangling 'An' in the spec is removed.

P5: bun test src and bunx vitest run pass with positive counts; tsc, lint and mise run tauri:check exit 0; mise run tauri:build produces web/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Kaiba.app whose Contents/MacOS/kaiba is byte-identical to the freshly built web/src-tauri/local-service/kaiba-aarch64-apple-darwin and newer than the build-start marker; the Swift diff against f02c4fe is empty.
nonGoals: No Swift, Rust, capability, tauri config, scripts or mise.toml change (D11).
No first-run modal, no in-place state reset, no credential pruning, no delete button for recent entries, no CSS edits.
No signing, notarization, release, git push or git write operations.
constraints: Do not touch the real store under the user's Application Support com.tacogips.kaiba/local directory; use tmp/ scratch directories for any runtime check.
Keep per-origin bearer scoping: a bearer under kaiba-note-bearer:<origin> is only sent to that origin; Local mode and the probe send no Authorization.

Existing tests keep passing unmodified; serverCredentialKey, currentServerCredentialKey, saveServerEndpoint, assertServerOrigin, serverRequest, normalizeServerEndpoint and readConnectionMode keep their behavior and signatures.
Files stay under 1000 lines; terse Solid/TS style; no emojis; do not modify unrelated files.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Five recent remote origins, most recent first, stored under kaiba-recent-server-endpoints; only a successful Remote save adds one, so tests and typos do not pollute the list.
Test connection checks /healthz for the kaiba service marker, then /graphql status only, and sends no bearer to any origin so it cannot leak credentials.
Test connection is advisory; saving an unreachable server is allowed because per-origin scoping makes a mistyped origin harmless.
Every save reloads the WebView to reset per-account in-memory state, as before.
No first-run chooser: the shell still renders on failure and the header Settings button and the login screen's compact form reach the connection settings.
Plain http to a non-loopback host warns but is not blocked, so LAN servers from iPhone keep working (D9).
No Swift or Rust change: /healthz, GraphQL 401 and the http/https capability already exist, and tauri:build already rebuilds the sidecar via beforeBuildCommand (D11, D12).
intentionalTradeoffs: Plain-http LAN endpoints remain allowed with a warning.
Credentials of origins evicted from the recent list are not pruned (pre-existing behavior).
The active connection line is computed at mount and only changes after the save reload.
Recent entries cannot be deleted individually.
supportedEdgeCases: Corrupt, non-array or non-string recent-list storage reads as [] without throwing; invalid entries are dropped and duplicates collapsed.
Re-recording an existing origin moves it to the front without duplication.
Loopback detection covers localhost, 127.x.x.x (including normalized 127.1) and [::1].

Probe maps network failure and timeout to unreachable, non-200 or non-kaiba healthz to not-kaiba, graphql 401 to auth-required, other statuses to server-error; validator errors propagate without any fetch.
Connection settings stay reachable when every client call fails with a network error and when the server answers 401.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Kaiba.app naming collision and distribution (pending in design-docs/user-qa/tauri-client-apps.md).
Redirect handling, retries or a third probe request.

Advisory, not blocking: a Recent servers pick clears the probe text but does not bump the probe generation counter (Step 5 low finding); the implementer may bump it for consistency without changing tests.
Advisory: grep -P is not portable to BSD grep; treat only exit 1 as no match in the P4 emoji check.
